assumptions.statement: The repository’s provisional overall boundary and three key areas are suitable only for concept discussion and internal recalculation.
assumptions.impact: All geometry, metrics, diagrams, and spatial claims must be recomputed after a cleared official boundary is supplied.

assumptions.statement: Land-use, building, public-space, green-space, road, and phase layers are agent-generated design propositions.
assumptions.impact: They do not describe existing conditions, ownership, confirmed construction, or statutory control.

assumptions.statement: No cleared parcel, existing-building, road-redline, municipal, heritage-control, engineering, ownership, or regulatory-control dataset is used.
assumptions.impact: Any physical implementation requires dedicated professional investigation and legal review.

assumptions.statement: Scenario cards, testing settings, and implementation phases are proposed operating protocols, not commitments by named institutions.
assumptions.impact: Partners, funding, consent procedures, and maintenance arrangements need separate confirmation.

assumptions.statement: Accessibility, human alternatives, and appeal paths are required in every proposed AI service.
assumptions.impact: A service that cannot meet these conditions should not expand beyond a prototype.

assumptions.statement: Cultural narratives and landmarks are interpretive design devices and make no claim about heritage protection status.
assumptions.impact: Formal heritage consultation is required before any material intervention.

assumptions.statement: Eight international cases are compared as methods for public-space, ecosystem, and operating interfaces; they are not copied as images, dimensions, performance claims, institutions, or local policy evidence.
assumptions.impact: Every translated move must be re-tested with Haidian users, public rules, and site data before implementation.

assumptions.statement: The original AI-generated cover is an editorial concept-atmosphere asset, not a depiction of an existing or approved Haidian condition.
assumptions.impact: All formal spatial claims remain in the GeoJSON, metrics, diagrams, and cited public sources.

assumptions.statement: The Open Ledger runner, its seven fixtures, and its result are package-contained synthetic tabletop evidence with no personal data, live service, named operator, contract, budget, deployment, or approval.
assumptions.impact: The runner can demonstrate that declared rejection gates work on fabricated records only; any real pilot needs separately confirmed site, rights, roles, permissions, professional review, restoration, and applicable legal procedures.

assumptions.statement: The original three-commons triptych only illustrates intended public relationships—arrival, understanding, co-editing, and return—and is not evidence of an existing or approved Haidian setting.
assumptions.impact: It must be read with the key-area diagram, scenario protocol, civic-scene evidence record, provisional geometry, and later professional/user review; it cannot establish site, scale, material, engineering, heritage, operator, or implementation claims.

assumptions.statement: The Commons Walk is a local, non-networked canvas interaction that compares the proposed civic relations and pause gates; it records no user behaviour and has no live data or site model.
assumptions.impact: It is an accessible reading aid only. Static drawings, structured evidence, cleared future inputs, and professional/user review remain necessary for every spatial, operational, engineering, heritage, and approval decision.
